speaker: Swami Sivananda
title: The practice of silence (Mouna)
text: Observe Mouna (vow of silence) for a couple of hours daily. Do not make gestures and inarticulate noises during the period of silence.
modern_interpretation: Commit to a daily practice of intentional silence, known as Mouna, for at least two hours. During this period, refrain not only from speaking but also from non-verbal communication like gestures or murmurs, allowing for deeper introspection and mental stillness in our increasingly noisy and distracting world.
summary: Practice a daily vow of complete silence, Mouna, for a few hours, refraining from all verbal and non-verbal communication, to cultivate inner peace and discipline.
actionable_advice: Designate a specific two-hour period daily to switch off all digital devices and refrain from speaking or gesturing, dedicating this time to quiet reflection or focused non-verbal tasks.
embedding_ready_text: Swami Sivananda's wisdom from 'The practice of silence (Mouna)' instructs us to 'Observe Mouna (vow of silence) for a couple of hours daily. Do not make gestures and inarticulate noises during the period of silence.' This timeless guidance addresses modern issues of overthinking, anxiety, restlessness, and digital distraction by fostering calm, self-awareness, and discipline. Practicing intentional silence for a designated period, completely refraining from verbal and non-verbal communication, cultivates mental stillness, sharpens focus, and offers a powerful tool for emotional regulation and self-inquiry, leading to deeper inner peace.
